authority: Declaration of what must be tracked, what may be present untracked, and what may be present ignored. Verified against real git state by scripts/check-inventory.cjs; it is not a self-report.
why: A broad .gitignore pattern can hide a file that must travel with the repository, so the loss is invisible to `git status` and to any review that counts status lines. This declaration makes that ignore surface explicit and checkable, and it keeps internal acceptance material out of the public surface.
notes: must_track_globs are files that MUST travel: every path matching them that is present on disk has to be tracked. They are the packaged schemas and the public contract vectors a clean clone needs to install and run.
A must-track glob may be added but the four required ones cannot be removed; scripts/check-inventory.cjs holds them, plus the forbidden-tracked globs, as hard invariants of its own.
allowed_ignored_globs is the reviewed exception list. Anything present but ignored that is not listed here is a failure, because it means the ignore surface changed without a declaration.

The first three allowed_ignored_globs are D1 rule (b) internal material: internal acceptance records carrying workstation/recovery paths. They are declared here so the ignore surface is a reviewable decision, and they are also forbidden-tracked in scripts/check-inventory.cjs so `git add -f` cannot publish them.
`**/node_modules/**` is depth-agnostic on purpose: npm workspaces install a second node_modules inside every packages/* directory, not only at the root.
allowed_untracked_globs is empty on purpose: this repository declares that a correct working tree has zero present-but-untracked files.
tracked_count is the exact number of tracked files. Re-pin it in the same change that adds or removes tracked files; the gate prints the command in its failure message.
